answer.why: Minister Salary is instantly clear and a bit cheeky, because everyone in Singapore has an opinion on ministers' pay. I'd tap it just to see if the game pokes fun at that. Confirmed & Substantive sounds like HR jargon I don't understand, so I'd scroll past.

answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: No idea honestly. Sounds like a boring civil service form or an HR email about job status. Maybe a serious office sim, but the name goes over my head and doesn't make me want to tap.

best_moment.what: Asking in Cabinet if ministers should be paid on indicators they set. Felt like the game's whole point, and it was the one time I got to poke at the pay thing I actually know about from the news.

worst_moment.what: PQ year again with only one option, answer straight. Same as the year before, no real choice, and my standing dropped anyway so it felt like tapping through a chore.

answer.held_back_by: Honestly nothing, I became PM. If anything it was my falling standing with voters, not the service. The ending card says my file had no ceiling, so I think the game just let me through because I stayed clean and took the hard jobs.
answer.ending_fair_why: I ended as PM with clean integrity, so it fits how I played. But the card reveals the ceiling and the Reshuffle choice only at the end, and I did not feel that choice was the big one when I made it. Still fair, just a bit of a surprise.
answer.chase_next: A run where I take the conglomerate board seat and pad the budget, to see if the cash and a worse integrity score gets a different ending, maybe a richer one but not PM.
answer.play_again_why: It was a long run and the last stretch was repetitive with the PQ years. I would come back another day to try the other path, not right now.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.
tone_breaks.note: Felt like the game smirking at the real pay debate, a little too pleased with itself. Also, PM pay at 2x seems like a detail I cannot check.

tone_breaks.line: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
tone_breaks.note: Funny, but it is the game nudging me that it is being clever.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was more about climbing grades, appraisals and being confirmed in roles than about the pay itself, and the ending was about the ceiling and the career. Minister Salary sounds catchier though.

DARREN LIM · THE FINAL POSITION
Prime Minister

You made it. The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.

RETIRED AS Prime Minister
AT AGE 59
LIFETIME EARNINGS $38.14M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Minister. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 45, in The Reshuffle, you chose "Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants." It raised your ceiling to Prime Minister.
